en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Monkey.
3. The Question on the Land-Tortoise “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one quality of the land-tortoise should be adopted,’ which is that one quality that should be adopted?
“Just as, O King, the land-tortoise, out of fear of water, wanders about avoiding water, and by that very avoidance of water it does not lose its life-span;”
In the same way, Great King, a yogi practicing yoga must see danger in negligence and see the excellence of qualities in heedfulness.
And by that seeing of danger, he does not fall away from the state of a recluse (sāmañña) and draws near to Nibbāna.
This, Great King, is one quality to be taken from the tortoise that carries its house on its back.
This too, O Great King, was spoken by the Blessed One, the God above gods, in the *Dhammapada*:
He is incapable of falling away;
he is indeed close to Nibbāna.
Thus ends the fourth question concerning the tortoise with a shell like a lotus leaf.
